evidence_summary: Surviving black Astrotone examples establish a February 1967 earliest known example and dated examples remain in production through 1969. The surviving service literature gives Universal Amplifier Corp. at 615 West 131st Street, New York City. This is strong model-specific evidence for Universal Amplifier manufacture.

The Sam Ash Fuzzz Boxx uses the same PCB and core production platform as the Astrotone. Surviving examples dated May 20-23 1967 and later 1969-coded examples support overlapping production rather than a simple successor relationship. Sam Ash was the marketed retail identity; Universal Amplifier is the physical builder.

evidence_summary: A later Sam Ash enclosure state is documented with the Astrotone-derived PCB platform and later-production construction clues. Surviving examples lack useful internal date stamps, so exact chronology versus other Fuzzz Boxx runs remains unresolved.

The original manual directs service returns to Universal Amplifier Corp. at 615 West 131st Street, New York City 10027. This independently ties the marketed Astro Amp product to the named corporation rather than merely inferring manufacture from circuit similarity.

A documented March 1967 Astrotone and May 1967 Sam Ash Fuzzz Boxx use identical boards and component platforms, demonstrating that Sam Ash branding was being produced in parallel with Astro Amp branding rather than replacing it immediately.

Fuzzboxes identifies a February 1967 earliest surviving Astrotone with Fairchild 2N3565 transistors and a subsequent March 1967 revision. This establishes period-specific internal production states that should not be collapsed into one undifferentiated Astrotone build.

May 20 and May 22 1967 Sam Ash examples document the revised Astrotone/Fuzzz Boxx platform after the earliest February and March Astrotone states. The evidence supports a shared production family with evolving component sets and enclosure treatments.

Potentiometer and internal date-code evidence places late examples into 1969. Exact final production date and the reason production ceased remain unknown, so the archive records 1969 as a latest evidenced production year rather than a hard end date.
